t: Subsection (e) of section 103 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 403–3) is amended to read as follows:“(e) Location of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.—The headquarters of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence may be located in the Washington metropolitan region, as that term is defined in section 8301 of title 40, United States Code.”.

fable.w: This provision only authorizes where the ODNI headquarters may be located. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The reference to the "Washington metropolitan region" is a geographic definition, not coordination with local governments.
fable.s: The headquarters of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence may be located in the Washington metropolitan region

qwen_block.w: This section simply defines the permissible geographic location for a federal agency's headquarters. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or interactions with states, tribes, or the public mentioned.
qwen_block.s: The headquarters of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence may be located in the Washington metropolitan region, as that term is defined in section 8301 of title 40, United States Code.

opus.w: This provision only allows the headquarters of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence to be located in the Washington metropolitan region. It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or advisory body involving outside parties. The reference to section 8301 of title 40 just supplies a geographic definition and does not bring any non-federal party into the decision.
opus.s: The headquarters of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence may be located in the Washington metropolitan region, as that term is defined in section 8301 of title 40, United States Code.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Section 8301 of title 40 involves regional planning, which could suggest outside regional bodies have a say. That doesn't hold up. The section only cites that law to define "Washington metropolitan region." It doesn't require any consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or advisory body before the headquarters location is decided. No one outside the federal government is involved.
